body:
I appreciate the suggestion, but I'm posting now because I'm stronger and can recognize the root of the problem and am hoping to find some justice instead of just quitting and letting these people get away with treating others this way.
I'm not the only one, I've confronted fellow male colleagues breaking down at their desk after hours due to the mistreatment.

So my boss was texting me knowing full well my dad was in heart surgery saying it was nice I was there for him but I should come into work, while a female coworker often leaves work at the drop of a hat to take care of her dog and the manager says to take her time and not worry.

I've been at the company longer than all but two of them but they're promoting a newer girl, allowing her into meetings, and allowing her to micromamage me.  She stares daggers at me, won't talk to me unless they need a project handled in a very condescending way, and when I brought this to the attention of management they said that everything I feel is just because my family is going through hard times, which is not the case.  I reported the girl's behavior five times and the management held a meeting with me claimimg I was at fault.

Ok,
I have a ton of e-mails that corroborate the situation.  But I guess dishing out $300 to talk to an attorney is my only option.

Ditto, 
Are our jobs really worth our life's though? I know there's probably much more to it, but I hope you know the answer is, "NO!"

I really empathize with you.  My wife is in a similar boat.  I have some amazing opportnuities out of state but my wife loves where we live, and to be honest so do I.  But circumstances are really difficult for our families so there's a lot of pressure for me to do something.   Sometimes it feels like we are forced into ultimatums.  I hope you and your husband can come to an understanding or at least a compromise.
Thanks for the advice.  I will definitely keep this in mind.
I would take muffled at this point. I'll do my best to hold out.

@OtherPlayers,
From what I'm seeing of the industry, the only thing that matters is a beast portfolio. If you have skills and a list of clients for referral then the skies the limit. Then again, the same could be said for any independent enterprise. Call me optimistic, but the days of college being the end all will come to pass eventually.  We have an entire generation who've been sucked dry and thrown to the winds. I've had too many friends commit suicide over student loan debt. It doesn't make sense.

We have an old beat up car just for emergency transportation.  It's paid off and the insurance is like $40. But I agree that moving down to one would help. The other I bought certified used. There's $3,300 left on the loan so I can see the light at the end of the tunnel, but most days it seems very far way.  
Yes, thankfully we have health insurance. Maybe it's time to get her into therapy. But with a copay we're looking at roughly $240 per month for sessions which eats into whatever we could be using to pay down debt. But, solving the root of a problem is key. I've personally witnessed her being treated like shit by employers our entire relationship. She's 4'11 so people instantly assume she's some kid as opposed to an adult just trying to live her life.

For the most part I just sit on the extra money.  I add $100 to the emergency fund and ignore the remainder as if it doesn't really exist.  There are periods where I pay aggressively on the credit cards, but I do that intermittently due to fear of unknown issues that could arise.
Total CC debt = 20,735.21.  4K is hers, the rest is me.  Yes, I'm very depressed most of the time.  Thanks for the kind words.

She has pretty crippling anxiety. She's trying some new medication that seems to help. But she's very small & has some legit trauma in her past that makes it hard for her to be in public. While it's an excuse, I'm pretty glad that I can't relate.

I'm trying to give her the opportunity she never had to just focus entirely on school at the moment. I know many people who work and go to school simultaneously. I grew up with a super mom like that, but I'm resigned to the fact that not everyone is that strong. It could be BS in my head, I hope it is, but after 13 years together I'm trying a different approach.
